Article 54

(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in protecting women and children from violence.

(2) Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted through: a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;

b. education and training for women and children victims of violence;

c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and

d. fostering and enhancing the economic independence of women victims of violence.

(3) Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be set forth in the form of an agreement.

Article 56

(1) The Regional Government is obliged to supervise the implementation of protection for women and children from violence.

(2) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be conducted with professional, transparent and accountable principles.

Article 59

(1) The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that implement protection for women and children from discrimination and violence.

(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with the regional financial capacity, and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the City of Bekasi.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Bekasi.
4. Regional Secretariat is the Regional Secretariat of the City of Bekasi.
5. Women are all women who are both within and outside the household.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old.
7. Protection is a form of service that must be carried out by law enforcement officers or security officers to provide a sense of security, both physical and mental to victims and sanctions from threats, disturbances, terror and violence from any party provided at the stage of investigation, inquiry, prosecution and examination in court proceedings.
8. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in fulfilling their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
9. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Empowerment of women is the effort of women to obtain access and control over resources, political economy, socio-culture, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems so as to be able to build their abilities and self-concept.
11. Gender and development is the equality of the role of women in development to the analysis of gender relations in access and control over resources and decision-making.
12. Gender equality and justice is the condition of social roles of women and men equally and fairly, through access, participation and control as well as benefits especially in development.
13. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of the entire process of planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of development program and activity policies.
14. Regional government affairs in the protection of women and children is by making planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluating development activities involving the role of women and children.
15. Economically weak women are women who have no income but have a high household economic burden but are responsible for meeting household economic needs.
16. Women working in the formal sector are those who receive protection of rights as workers in laws and regulations and receive tax obligations.
17. Women as heads of households are women who bear the burden of household needs including child care.
18. Women and reproductive health are women who must have the right to obtain reproductive health and understanding of reproductive health.
19. Women and violence is any action that violates, obstructs, eliminates enjoyment and ignores the human rights of women.
20. Community participation in the protection of women is the participation of the community individually or institutionally in the community, responsible for the protection of children and protection of women.
21. Child Worker is a child who performs work on his/her own behalf, with others and/or with Employers.
22. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social.
23. Street children are children whose lives are irregular by spending most of their time earning a living and or in other public places.
24. Right is about something that is correct, property, ownership, authority and power to do something.
25. Guarantee is liability.
26. Parents are biological Father and/or Mother, step Father and/or Mother, adoptive Father and/or Mother.
27. Family is a person who has a blood relationship upward/downward up to the third degree or has a marriage relationship or a person who has dependents either women and/or children.
28. Community is individuals, families, groups and/or community organizations.

Article 47

The Regional Government is obliged to provide complaint services for the protection of women and children from acts of violence, trafficking and exploitation.

Article 14

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide facilities and conduct comprehensive health efforts for women in order to obtain optimal health status.

(2) The provision of facilities and implementation of comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation.

(3) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts for both basic health and referral.

(4) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted free of charge for persons with disabilities, victims of violence, kidnapping, neglect, HIV/AIDS transmission, those economically and sexually exploited, trafficking.

(5) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted gradually in accordance with regional financial capacity.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the City of Bekasi.

Protection is a form of service that must be carried out by law enforcement officers or security officers to provide a sense of security, both physical and mental to victims and sanctions from threats, disturbances, terror and violence from any party provided at the stage of investigation, inquiry, prosecution and examination in court proceedings.
8. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in fulfilling their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
9. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

22. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social.
23. Street children are children whose lives are irregular by spending most of their time earning a living and or in other public places.
24. Right is about something that is correct, property, ownership, authority and power to do something.
25. Guarantee is liability.
26. Parents are biological Father and/or Mother, step Father and/or Mother, adoptive Father and/or Mother.
27. Family is a person who has a blood relationship upward/downward up to the third degree or has a marriage relationship or a person who has dependents either women and/or children.
28. Community is individuals, families, groups and/or community organizations.

d. fostering and enhancing the economic independence of women victims of violence.

(3) Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be set forth in the form of an agreement.

Article 43

The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 40 letters c and d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

In addition to P2TP2A as referred to in Article 6 and KPAID as referred to in Article 8, to support the implementation of protection for women and children from violence, human trafficking and exploitation, involves the Task Force on the Crime of Human Trafficking (TPPO).

The Regional Government is obliged to provide complaint services for the protection of women and children from acts of violence, trafficking and exploitation.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the City of Bekasi.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Bekasi.
4. Regional Secretariat is the Regional Secretariat of the City of Bekasi.
5. Women are all women who are both within and outside the household.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old.
7. Protection is a form of service that must be carried out by law enforcement officers or security officers to provide a sense of security, both physical and mental to victims and sanctions from threats, disturbances, terror and violence from any party provided at the stage of investigation, inquiry, prosecution and examination in court proceedings.
8. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in fulfilling their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
9. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Empowerment of women is the effort of women to obtain access and control over resources, political economy, socio-culture, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems so as to be able to build their abilities and self-concept.
11. Gender and development is the equality of the role of women in development to the analysis of gender relations in access and control over resources and decision-making.
12. Gender equality and justice is the condition of social roles of women and men equally and fairly, through access, participation and control as well as benefits especially in development.
13. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of the entire process of planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of development program and activity policies.
14. Regional government affairs in the protection of women and children is by making planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluating development activities involving the role of women and children.
15. Economically weak women are women who have no income but have a high household economic burden but are responsible for meeting household economic needs.
16. Women working in the formal sector are those who receive protection of rights as workers in laws and regulations and receive tax obligations.
17. Women as heads of households are women who bear the burden of household needs including child care.
18. Women and reproductive health are women who must have the right to obtain reproductive health and understanding of reproductive health.
19. Women and violence is any action that violates, obstructs, eliminates enjoyment and ignores the human rights of women.
20. Community participation in the protection of women is the participation of the community individually or institutionally in the community, responsible for the protection of children and protection of women.
21. Child Worker is a child who performs work on his/her own behalf, with others and/or with Employers.
22. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social.
23. Street children are children whose lives are irregular by spending most of their time earning a living and or in other public places.
24. Right is about something that is correct, property, ownership, authority and power to do something.
25. Guarantee is liability.
26. Parents are biological Father and/or Mother, step Father and/or Mother, adoptive Father and/or Mother.
27. Family is a person who has a blood relationship upward/downward up to the third degree or has a marriage relationship or a person who has dependents either women and/or children.
28. Community is individuals, families, groups and/or community organizations.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the City of Bekasi.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Bekasi.
4. Regional Secretariat is the Regional Secretariat of the City of Bekasi.
5. Women are all women who are both within and outside the household.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old.
7. Protection is a form of service that must be carried out by law enforcement officers or security officers to provide a sense of security, both physical and mental to victims and sanctions from threats, disturbances, terror and violence from any party provided at the stage of investigation, inquiry, prosecution and examination in court proceedings.
8. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in fulfilling their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
9. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Empowerment of women is the effort of women to obtain access and control over resources, political economy, socio-culture, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems so as to be able to build their abilities and self-concept.
11. Gender and development is the equality of the role of women in development to the analysis of gender relations in access and control over resources and decision-making.
12. Gender equality and justice is the condition of social roles of women and men equally and fairly, through access, participation and control as well as benefits especially in development.
13. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of the entire process of planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of development program and activity policies.
14. Regional government affairs in the protection of women and children is by making planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluating development activities involving the role of women and children.
15. Economically weak women are women who have no income but have a high household economic burden but are responsible for meeting household economic needs.
16. Women working in the formal sector are those who receive protection of rights as workers in laws and regulations and receive tax obligations.
17. Women as heads of households are women who bear the burden of household needs including child care.
18. Women and reproductive health are women who must have the right to obtain reproductive health and understanding of reproductive health.
19. Women and violence is any action that violates, obstructs, eliminates enjoyment and ignores the human rights of women.
20. Community participation in the protection of women is the participation of the community individually or institutionally in the community, responsible for the protection of children and protection of women.
21. Child Worker is a child who performs work on his/her own behalf, with others and/or with Employers.
22. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social.
23. Street children are children whose lives are irregular by spending most of their time earning a living and or in other public places.
24. Right is about something that is correct, property, ownership, authority and power to do something.
25. Guarantee is liability.
26. Parents are biological Father and/or Mother, step Father and/or Mother, adoptive Father and/or Mother.
27. Family is a person who has a blood relationship upward/downward up to the third degree or has a marriage relationship or a person who has dependents either women and/or children.
28. Community is individuals, families, groups and/or community organizations.

Article 11

The community is obligated and responsible for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the implementation of the protection of women and children.

Article 14

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide facilities and conduct comprehensive health efforts for women in order to obtain optimal health status.

(2) The provision of facilities and implementation of comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation.

(3) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts for both basic health and referral.

(4) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted free of charge for persons with disabilities, victims of violence, kidnapping, neglect, HIV/AIDS transmission, those economically and sexually exploited, trafficking.

(5) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted gradually in accordance with regional financial capacity.

CHAPTER XIX

Article 57

The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children from violence organized by the Regional Government through the mechanism of conveying aspirations to the Mayor or to the DPRD.

Article 21

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide facilities and conduct comprehensive health efforts for children in order to obtain optimal health status starting from the womb.

(2) The provision of facilities and implementation of comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation.

(3) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts for both basic health and referral.

(4) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted free of charge for persons with disabilities, street children, children who are victims of violence, kidnapping, abandoned children, HIV/AIDS transmission, those economically and sexually exploited, trafficking, abuse of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances (NAFZA) from poor families.

(5) Children receive a guarantee to receive exclusive breastfeeding from their Mother in a proper and reasonable manner.

(6) For children from underprivileged families, the Government facilitates and provides nutritional assistance or supplementary food to improve children's health.

(7) To ensure the implementation of Children's rights as referred to in paragraph (5) above, the Government is obligated to facilitate infrastructure and facilities for breastfeeding at least in public service places.

(8) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted gradually in accordance with regional financial capacity.

Article 19

(1) Protection of women in marriage is that women receive legal protection and are based on their rights as women.

(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with the regional financial capacity, and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 54

(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in protecting women and children from violence.

(2) Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted through: a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;

b. education and training for women and children victims of violence;

c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and

d. fostering and enhancing the economic independence of women victims of violence.

Article 11

The community is obligated and responsible for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the implementation of the protection of women and children.

2.6.text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the City of Bekasi.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Bekasi.
4. Regional Secretariat is the Regional Secretariat of the City of Bekasi.
5. Women are all women who are both within and outside the household.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old.
7. Protection is a form of service that must be carried out by law enforcement officers or security officers to provide a sense of security, both physical and mental to victims and sanctions from threats, disturbances, terror and violence from any party provided at the stage of investigation, inquiry, prosecution and examination in court proceedings.
8. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in fulfilling their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
9. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Empowerment of women is the effort of women to obtain access and control over resources, political economy, socio-culture, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems so as to be able to build their abilities and self-concept.
11. Gender and development is the equality of the role of women in development to the analysis of gender relations in access and control over resources and decision-making.
12. Gender equality and justice is the condition of social roles of women and men equally and fairly, through access, participation and control as well as benefits especially in development.
13. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of the entire process of planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of development program and activity policies.
14. Regional government affairs in the protection of women and children is by making planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluating development activities involving the role of women and children.
15. Economically weak women are women who have no income but have a high household economic burden but are responsible for meeting household economic needs.
16. Women working in the formal sector are those who receive protection of rights as workers in laws and regulations and receive tax obligations.
17. Women as heads of households are women who bear the burden of household needs including child care.
18. Women and reproductive health are women who must have the right to obtain reproductive health and understanding of reproductive health.
19. Women and violence is any action that violates, obstructs, eliminates enjoyment and ignores the human rights of women.
20. Community participation in the protection of women is the participation of the community individually or institutionally in the community, responsible for the protection of children and protection of women.
21. Child Worker is a child who performs work on his/her own behalf, with others and/or with Employers.
22. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social.
23. Street children are children whose lives are irregular by spending most of their time earning a living and or in other public places.
24. Right is about something that is correct, property, ownership, authority and power to do something.
25. Guarantee is liability.
26. Parents are biological Father and/or Mother, step Father and/or Mother, adoptive Father and/or Mother.
27. Family is a person who has a blood relationship upward/downward up to the third degree or has a marriage relationship or a person who has dependents either women and/or children.
28. Community is individuals, families, groups and/or community organizations.

Article 14

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide facilities and conduct comprehensive health efforts for women in order to obtain optimal health status.

(2) The provision of facilities and implementation of comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation.

(3) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts for both basic health and referral.

(4) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted free of charge for persons with disabilities, victims of violence, kidnapping, neglect, HIV/AIDS transmission, those economically and sexually exploited, trafficking.

(5) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted gradually in accordance with regional financial capacity.

Article 21

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide facilities and conduct comprehensive health efforts for children in order to obtain optimal health status starting from the womb.

(2) The provision of facilities and implementation of comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation.

(3) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts for both basic health and referral.

(4) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted free of charge for persons with disabilities, street children, children who are victims of violence, kidnapping, abandoned children, HIV/AIDS transmission, those economically and sexually exploited, trafficking, abuse of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances (NAFZA) from poor families.

(5) Children receive a guarantee to receive exclusive breastfeeding from their Mother in a proper and reasonable manner.

(6) For children from underprivileged families, the Government facilitates and provides nutritional assistance or supplementary food to improve children's health.

(7) To ensure the implementation of Children's rights as referred to in paragraph (5) above, the Government is obligated to facilitate infrastructure and facilities for breastfeeding at least in public service places.

(8) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted gradually in accordance with regional financial capacity.

Article 24

(1) The Regional Government guarantees the implementation of a compulsory education program of at least 9 (nine) years for all children.

(2) The implementation of the compulsory education program as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation and the business sector.

(3) Parents and family are obligated to provide the widest possible opportunity to children according to the child's ability to obtain education.

(4) Every education provider is prohibited from expelling children from educational institutions without a guarantee for the continuity of the child's education.

(5) The implementation of the compulsory education program as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated in a separate regional regulation.

The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children from violence organized by the Regional Government through the mechanism of conveying aspirations to the Mayor or to the DPRD.

Article 56

(1) The Regional Government is obliged to supervise the implementation of protection for women and children from violence.

(2) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be conducted with professional, transparent and accountable principles.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the City of Bekasi.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Bekasi.
4. Regional Secretariat is the Regional Secretariat of the City of Bekasi.
5. Women are all women who are both within and outside the household.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old.
7. Protection is a form of service that must be carried out by law enforcement officers or security officers to provide a sense of security, both physical and mental to victims and sanctions from threats, disturbances, terror and violence from any party provided at the stage of investigation, inquiry, prosecution and examination in court proceedings.
8. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in fulfilling their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
9. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Empowerment of women is the effort of women to obtain access and control over resources, political economy, socio-culture, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems so as to be able to build their abilities and self-concept.
11. Gender and development is the equality of the role of women in development to the analysis of gender relations in access and control over resources and decision-making.
12. Gender equality and justice is the condition of social roles of women and men equally and fairly, through access, participation and control as well as benefits especially in development.
13. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of the entire process of planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of development program and activity policies.
14. Regional government affairs in the protection of women and children is by making planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluating development activities involving the role of women and children.
15. Economically weak women are women who have no income but have a high household economic burden but are responsible for meeting household economic needs.
16. Women working in the formal sector are those who receive protection of rights as workers in laws and regulations and receive tax obligations.
17. Women as heads of households are women who bear the burden of household needs including child care.
18. Women and reproductive health are women who must have the right to obtain reproductive health and understanding of reproductive health.
19. Women and violence is any action that violates, obstructs, eliminates enjoyment and ignores the human rights of women.
20. Community participation in the protection of women is the participation of the community individually or institutionally in the community, responsible for the protection of children and protection of women.
21. Child Worker is a child who performs work on his/her own behalf, with others and/or with Employers.
22. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social.
23. Street children are children whose lives are irregular by spending most of their time earning a living and or in other public places.
24. Right is about something that is correct, property, ownership, authority and power to do something.
25. Guarantee is liability.
26. Parents are biological Father and/or Mother, step Father and/or Mother, adoptive Father and/or Mother.
27. Family is a person who has a blood relationship upward/downward up to the third degree or has a marriage relationship or a person who has dependents either women and/or children.
28. Community is individuals, families, groups and/or community organizations.

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE MAYOR OF BEKASI,

Considering : a. that in order to guarantee and protect the rights of women and children so that they can participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence, discrimination and other violations of the rights of women and children, it is necessary to undertake efforts to protect women and children; b. that in order for efforts to protect women and children to obtain optimal results, there is a need for concrete actions from the Regional

Government and to enhance broad community participation; c. that based on the considerations as referred to in letters a and b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Protection of

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the City of Bekasi.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Bekasi.
4. Regional Secretariat is the Regional Secretariat of the City of Bekasi.
5. Women are all women who are both within and outside the household.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old.
7. Protection is a form of service that must be carried out by law enforcement officers or security officers to provide a sense of security, both physical and mental to victims and sanctions from threats, disturbances, terror and violence from any party provided at the stage of investigation, inquiry, prosecution and examination in court proceedings.
8. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in fulfilling their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
9. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Empowerment of women is the effort of women to obtain access and control over resources, political economy, socio-culture, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems so as to be able to build their abilities and self-concept.
11. Gender and development is the equality of the role of women in development to the analysis of gender relations in access and control over resources and decision-making.
12. Gender equality and justice is the condition of social roles of women and men equally and fairly, through access, participation and control as well as benefits especially in development.
13. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of the entire process of planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of development program and activity policies.
14. Regional government affairs in the protection of women and children is by making planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluating development activities involving the role of women and children.
15. Economically weak women are women who have no income but have a high household economic burden but are responsible for meeting household economic needs.
16. Women working in the formal sector are those who receive protection of rights as workers in laws and regulations and receive tax obligations.
17. Women as heads of households are women who bear the burden of household needs including child care.
18. Women and reproductive health are women who must have the right to obtain reproductive health and understanding of reproductive health.
19. Women and violence is any action that violates, obstructs, eliminates enjoyment and ignores the human rights of women.
20. Community participation in the protection of women is the participation of the community individually or institutionally in the community, responsible for the protection of children and protection of women.
21. Child Worker is a child who performs work on his/her own behalf, with others and/or with Employers.
22. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social.
23. Street children are children whose lives are irregular by spending most of their time earning a living and or in other public places.
24. Right is about something that is correct, property, ownership, authority and power to do something.
25. Guarantee is liability.
26. Parents are biological Father and/or Mother, step Father and/or Mother, adoptive Father and/or Mother.
27. Family is a person who has a blood relationship upward/downward up to the third degree or has a marriage relationship or a person who has dependents either women and/or children.
28. Community is individuals, families, groups and/or community organizations.

Article 48

The Regional Government and the community or social service institutions may establish recovery houses or safe houses.

Article 34

(1) Guardianship is a guarantee of protection for children to continue their lives towards adulthood.

(2) Child guardianship is intended to properly guarantee children's rights.

(3) Guardianship is carried out in the event that parents are not competent in legal actions, their whereabouts and residence are unknown.

(4) Guardianship referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) above is carried out through court determination.

(5) Guardianship for abandoned children is carried out with the permission of the Regional Government through related agencies.

(6) Guardianship of children who experience violence is carried out with the permission of the parents or child's family and acknowledged by the Regional Government through related agencies.

Article 19

(1) Protection of women in marriage is that women receive legal protection and are based on their rights as women.

(2) The implementation of protection for women in marriage is conducted by the Ministry of Religious Affairs, namely the Religious Affairs Office (KUA) which is responsible for the implementation of marriages.

(3) The responsibility of KUA for the protection of women in marriage includes:

a. supervising the conduct of marriages under religious and state law;
b. socializing the prohibition of unregistered marriages (nikah sirih) which can harm women and children;
c. canceling marriages that do not go through legitimate legal processes both religiously and by the State.
(4) The Regional Government may conduct mass marriage activities for underprivileged couples free of charge.

Article 54

(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in protecting women and children from violence.

(2) Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted through: a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;

b. education and training for women and children victims of violence;

c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and

d. fostering and enhancing the economic independence of women victims of violence.

(3) Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be set forth in the form of an agreement.

Article 14

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide facilities and conduct comprehensive health efforts for women in order to obtain optimal health status.

(2) The provision of facilities and implementation of comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation.

(3) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts for both basic health and referral.

(4) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted free of charge for persons with disabilities, victims of violence, kidnapping, neglect, HIV/AIDS transmission, those economically and sexually exploited, trafficking.

(5) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted gradually in accordance with regional financial capacity.

Article 21

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide facilities and conduct comprehensive health efforts for children in order to obtain optimal health status starting from the womb.

(2) The provision of facilities and implementation of comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation.

(3) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts for both basic health and referral.

(4) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted free of charge for persons with disabilities, street children, children who are victims of violence, kidnapping, abandoned children, HIV/AIDS transmission, those economically and sexually exploited, trafficking, abuse of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances (NAFZA) from poor families.

(5) Children receive a guarantee to receive exclusive breastfeeding from their Mother in a proper and reasonable manner.

(6) For children from underprivileged families, the Government facilitates and provides nutritional assistance or supplementary food to improve children's health.

(7) To ensure the implementation of Children's rights as referred to in paragraph (5) above, the Government is obligated to facilitate infrastructure and facilities for breastfeeding at least in public service places.

(8) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted gradually in accordance with regional financial capacity.

Article 31

(1) Child care is the obligation of parents, community and Government.

(2) Family care is the first and foremost care for children.

(3) Community care for children may be carried out individually and/or institutionally.

(4) Institutionally it may be organized through Social Child Care Institutions.

(5) Social Child Care Institutions as referred to in paragraph (4) must obtain permission from the Regional Government through related agencies.

(6) The Government carries out child care through: a. formulation of child protection policies to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights;

b. providing facilities and infrastructure for Social Child Care Institutions; c. if Regional Government-owned Social Child Care Institutions are not yet available, may refer to the nearest Government-owned PSAA in accordance with the needs of the child;

d. providing budget for maintaining a safe and comfortable environment for optimal child growth and development through the development of Child-Friendly City of Bekasi.

Article 33

(1) To assist the smooth implementation of the duties of the Child-Friendly City Task Force, a secretariat is formed.

(2) The Secretariat of the Child-Friendly City Task Force is facilitated by the Regional Government.

(3) The formation of the secretariat and secretariat personnel of the Child-Friendly City Task Force is stipulated by the Mayor.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the City of Bekasi.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Bekasi.
4. Regional Secretariat is the Regional Secretariat of the City of Bekasi.
5. Women are all women who are both within and outside the household.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old.
7. Protection is a form of service that must be carried out by law enforcement officers or security officers to provide a sense of security, both physical and mental to victims and sanctions from threats, disturbances, terror and violence from any party provided at the stage of investigation, inquiry, prosecution and examination in court proceedings.
8. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in fulfilling their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
9. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Empowerment of women is the effort of women to obtain access and control over resources, political economy, socio-culture, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems so as to be able to build their abilities and self-concept.
11. Gender and development is the equality of the role of women in development to the analysis of gender relations in access and control over resources and decision-making.
12. Gender equality and justice is the condition of social roles of women and men equally and fairly, through access, participation and control as well as benefits especially in development.
13. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of the entire process of planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of development program and activity policies.
14. Regional government affairs in the protection of women and children is by making planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluating development activities involving the role of women and children.
15. Economically weak women are women who have no income but have a high household economic burden but are responsible for meeting household economic needs.
16. Women working in the formal sector are those who receive protection of rights as workers in laws and regulations and receive tax obligations.
17. Women as heads of households are women who bear the burden of household needs including child care.
18. Women and reproductive health are women who must have the right to obtain reproductive health and understanding of reproductive health.
19. Women and violence is any action that violates, obstructs, eliminates enjoyment and ignores the human rights of women.
20. Community participation in the protection of women is the participation of the community individually or institutionally in the community, responsible for the protection of children and protection of women.
21. Child Worker is a child who performs work on his/her own behalf, with others and/or with Employers.
22. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social.
23. Street children are children whose lives are irregular by spending most of their time earning a living and or in other public places.
24. Right is about something that is correct, property, ownership, authority and power to do something.
25. Guarantee is liability.
26. Parents are biological Father and/or Mother, step Father and/or Mother, adoptive Father and/or Mother.
27. Family is a person who has a blood relationship upward/downward up to the third degree or has a marriage relationship or a person who has dependents either women and/or children.
28. Community is individuals, families, groups and/or community organizations.

Article 31

(1) Child care is the obligation of parents, community and Government.

(2) Family care is the first and foremost care for children.

(3) Community care for children may be carried out individually and/or institutionally.

(4) Institutionally it may be organized through Social Child Care Institutions.

(5) Social Child Care Institutions as referred to in paragraph (4) must obtain permission from the Regional Government through related agencies.

(6) The Government carries out child care through: a. formulation of child protection policies to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights;

b. providing facilities and infrastructure for Social Child Care Institutions; c. if Regional Government-owned Social Child Care Institutions are not yet available, may refer to the nearest Government-owned PSAA in accordance with the needs of the child;

d. providing budget for maintaining a safe and comfortable environment for optimal child growth and development through the development of Child-Friendly City of Bekasi.

CHAPTER VI

Article 21

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide facilities and conduct comprehensive health efforts for children in order to obtain optimal health status starting from the womb.

(2) The provision of facilities and implementation of comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation.

(3) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts for both basic health and referral.

(4) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted free of charge for persons with disabilities, street children, children who are victims of violence, kidnapping, abandoned children, HIV/AIDS transmission, those economically and sexually exploited, trafficking, abuse of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances (NAFZA) from poor families.

(5) Children receive a guarantee to receive exclusive breastfeeding from their Mother in a proper and reasonable manner.

(6) For children from underprivileged families, the Government facilitates and provides nutritional assistance or supplementary food to improve children's health.

(7) To ensure the implementation of Children's rights as referred to in paragraph (5) above, the Government is obligated to facilitate infrastructure and facilities for breastfeeding at least in public service places.

(8) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted gradually in accordance with regional financial capacity.

Article 14

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide facilities and conduct comprehensive health efforts for women in order to obtain optimal health status.

(2) The provision of facilities and implementation of comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation.

(3) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts for both basic health and referral.

(4) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted free of charge for persons with disabilities, victims of violence, kidnapping, neglect, HIV/AIDS transmission, those economically and sexually exploited, trafficking.

(5) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted gradually in accordance with regional financial capacity.

Article 27

(2) The implementation of Early Childhood Education Post (PAUD) by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) above shall be carried out in accordance with regional financial capacity.

Article 19

(1) Protection of women in marriage is that women receive legal protection and are based on their rights as women.

(2) The implementation of protection for women in marriage is conducted by the Ministry of Religious Affairs, namely the Religious Affairs Office (KUA) which is responsible for the implementation of marriages.

(3) The responsibility of KUA for the protection of women in marriage includes:

a. supervising the conduct of marriages under religious and state law;
b. socializing the prohibition of unregistered marriages (nikah sirih) which can harm women and children;
c. canceling marriages that do not go through legitimate legal processes both religiously and by the State.
(4) The Regional Government may conduct mass marriage activities for underprivileged couples free of charge.

Article 54

(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in protecting women and children from violence.

(2) Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted through: a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;

b. education and training for women and children victims of violence;

c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and

d. fostering and enhancing the economic independence of women victims of violence.

(3) Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be set forth in the form of an agreement.

Article 58

Financing for the implementation of protection for women and children from violence is sourced from:

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD); and
b. other legitimate sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 59

(1) The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that implement protection for women and children from discrimination and violence.

(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with the regional financial capacity, and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 14

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide facilities and conduct comprehensive health efforts for women in order to obtain optimal health status.

(2) The provision of facilities and implementation of comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation.

(3) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts for both basic health and referral.

(4) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted free of charge for persons with disabilities, victims of violence, kidnapping, neglect, HIV/AIDS transmission, those economically and sexually exploited, trafficking.

(5) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted gradually in accordance with regional financial capacity.

Article 31

(1) Child care is the obligation of parents, community and Government.

(2) Family care is the first and foremost care for children.

(3) Community care for children may be carried out individually and/or institutionally.

(4) Institutionally it may be organized through Social Child Care Institutions.

(5) Social Child Care Institutions as referred to in paragraph (4) must obtain permission from the Regional Government through related agencies.

(6) The Government carries out child care through: a. formulation of child protection policies to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights;

b. providing facilities and infrastructure for Social Child Care Institutions; c. if Regional Government-owned Social Child Care Institutions are not yet available, may refer to the nearest Government-owned PSAA in accordance with the needs of the child;

d. providing budget for maintaining a safe and comfortable environment for optimal child growth and development through the development of Child-Friendly City of Bekasi.

Article 21

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide facilities and conduct comprehensive health efforts for children in order to obtain optimal health status starting from the womb.

(2) The provision of facilities and implementation of comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation.

(3) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts for both basic health and referral.

(4) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted free of charge for persons with disabilities, street children, children who are victims of violence, kidnapping, abandoned children, HIV/AIDS transmission, those economically and sexually exploited, trafficking, abuse of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances (NAFZA) from poor families.

(5) Children receive a guarantee to receive exclusive breastfeeding from their Mother in a proper and reasonable manner.

(6) For children from underprivileged families, the Government facilitates and provides nutritional assistance or supplementary food to improve children's health.

(7) To ensure the implementation of Children's rights as referred to in paragraph (5) above, the Government is obligated to facilitate infrastructure and facilities for breastfeeding at least in public service places.

(8) Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted gradually in accordance with regional financial capacity.

Article 24

(1) The Regional Government guarantees the implementation of a compulsory education program of at least 9 (nine) years for all children.

(2) The implementation of the compulsory education program as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation and the business sector.

(3) Parents and family are obligated to provide the widest possible opportunity to children according to the child's ability to obtain education.

(4) Every education provider is prohibited from expelling children from educational institutions without a guarantee for the continuity of the child's education.

(5) The implementation of the compulsory education program as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated in a separate regional regulation.
